# Vendored third-party headers

This directory holds the two single-source dependencies of the runtime, vendored
so the project builds without relying on system-installed copies (VMA is *not*
packaged on Debian; Vulkan-Hpp is vendored to pin an exact, SDK-matched version).

The vendored headers are **git-ignored** (see the repo root `.gitignore`) and
regenerated by `scripts/fetch_third_party.sh`. Run that script after a fresh
clone, before configuring.

| Header | Version | License | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vma/vk_mem_alloc.h` | **3.4.0** (`VMA_VERSION = VK_MAKE_VERSION(3, 4, 0)`) | MIT (AMD) | <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/master/include/vk_mem_alloc.h> |
| `vulkan-hpp/vulkan/*.hpp` | **Vulkan 1.4.309** (`VK_HEADER_VERSION == 309`; no `VULKAN_HPP_VERSION` macro — version is tracked by `VK_HEADER_VERSION`) | Apache-2.0 OR MIT (Khronos) | <https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Hpp> tag `v1.4.309` |

## Vulkan-Hpp version pinning (important)

The `vulkan.hpp` header contains
`static_assert( VK_HEADER_VERSION == <N>, ... )`, which must match the Vulkan C
headers (`vulkan_core.h`) shipped by the Vulkan SDK / system package. The
installed SDK here is **1.4.309**, so the matching Vulkan-Hpp tag `v1.4.309`
was vendored. The `main` branch of Vulkan-Hpp tracks a newer header version
(e.g. `VK_HEADER_VERSION == 360` at the time of writing) and would **fail to
compile** against the 1.4.309 SDK. Do not "upgrade" these headers without also
upgrading the Vulkan SDK (or vice-versa).

## Provenance / layout

- Vulkan-Hpp is vendored in the upstream `include/` layout, i.e.
  `vulkan-hpp/vulkan/*.hpp`, so `#include <vulkan/vulkan.hpp>` resolves through
  the `third_party/vulkan-hpp` include directory *before* the system
  `/usr/include`. The Vulkan **C** headers (`vulkan.h`, `vulkan_core.h`, …) are
  *not* vendored — they come from the SDK via the `Vulkan::Vulkan` target.
- VMA is a single self-contained header, included as `#include <vk_mem_alloc.h>`
  from `third_party/vma`. Configure it with `VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS=0` and
  `VMA_DYNAMIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS=1` so it resolves Vulkan entry points through
  `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` / `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` at runtime.
